column1: # split_reader_v2 — measured DEVICE KERNEL DURATION [ns], Wormhole B0
# box: bgd-lab-16-special-dstoiljkovic (12 DRAM banks, 64 L1 banks), profiler ON.
# One fresh-cache measured launch per (plan, arm); launch 1 of each pair is the
# compile warm-up AND the bit-exact correctness gate (torch.equal). EVERY arm
# listed here was bit-exact; L1_OOM rows never ran (the CBs do not fit).
# Repeat sessions of the same cell are listed as `a/b/c` (session spread <= 1.5%).
#   op_baseline        NCRISC reads all blocks (library read_sticks_for_tilize),
#                      compute = ONE helper call for the core, BRISC drains.
#   nodrain            as op_baseline, nobody drains the aliased output CB.
#   alt_tax            ONE reader, ONE CB, but compute in the per-block
#                      back-to-back helper form the split forces on it.
#   raw_baseline       ONE reader, raw noc_async_read instead of the helper.
#   split_il           dedicated dual-NoC, stride-2 interleave 50/50, no drain.
#   split_il_cdrain    ditto, COMPUTE drains  <-- L1-SOURCE INTEGRATION FORM
#   split_il_bdrain    ditto, BRISC reads AND drains.
#   split_p57/60/67/75 dedicated dual-NoC, PERIODIC weighted interleave, NCRISC's
#   split_w75          Perf-1's CONTIGUOUS 3:1 split (CB depth = half the core's
#                      blocks -> L1 scales with the tensor; not integrable).
#   split_trid         BOTH DM RISCs on NOC_0 (DM_DYNAMIC_NOC) + per-RISC read
#   split_trid_cdrain  ditto, COMPUTE drains   <-- DRAM-SOURCE INTEGRATION FORM
#   split_rw / _p88    interleaved destination: BRISC keeps the WRITES and takes
# ---------- FOCUS PLAN 1: DRAM -> HEIGHT-sharded L1, 8 cores ----------
# ---------- FOCUS PLAN 2: WIDTH-sharded L1 (2 cores) -> HEIGHT-sharded L1 (8) ----------
# ---------- DOMAIN: DRAM source, destination-local. Read-transfer ladder. ----------
# ---------- plans the REAL OP does NOT route destination-local (xfer_gate) ----------
# The bench forces the destination-local path; the op's MIN_STREAM_READ_BYTES gate
# sends both of these to the 64-core interleaved split instead (which is why the
# anchor is much faster than the bench baseline). Recorded, but NOT domain evidence.
# ---------- THE EXCLUSION: interleaved DESTINATION (BRISC issues the writes) ----------
# ---------- derived: achieved READ bandwidth (tensor bytes / ns, 8 cores) ------
# The mechanism, not an argument. The split only pays where the baseline read is
# ISSUE-bound; it never beats the fabric.
# crossover_512         126.6            135.2   <- already at the ceiling: FLAT
# crossover_fp32        124.9            131.1   <- already at the ceiling: FLAT
# crossover_wide        152.5            130.6   <- above it: the split LOSES
# crossover_2048        143.6              -     <- above it, and CBs do not fit
